\caption{Thread scaling at four workers against voluntary context switches of the server per request (GIL build, 400 connections; bars are 95\% half-widths; the grey line marks no gain over one worker, the dashed line the scaling of the C loop run as processes). Shown are the thread-mode configurations of Tables~\ref{tab:factorial}, \ref{tab:scaling}, \ref{tab:app} and~\ref{tab:gilbatch}, an engine that appears in two of them once. The connected points are one reactor with the number of requests served per GIL acquisition varied. The arrows mark two interventions: the Python loop on \code{epoll} with its releases batched, and the \code{epoll} reactor taking the GIL per batch instead of per request. For \code{asyncio} and \code{uvloop} the request count is the client's.}
\label{fig:handoffs}
